userStories.title: Honor JWT lifetimes in browser cookies and SSR refresh
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Align browser cookie scheduling with each JWT's expiry and recover eligible SSR navigations carrying an expired legacy access cookie.

**Motivation** — A five-minute access JWT still has a browser cookie at minute six.

**Approach** — The API signs each access and refresh JWT with its own NumericDate `exp` using the configured lifetimes in `apps/api/src/config/auth.config.ts` and `apps/api/src/auth/auth.module.ts`. At the existing common `setAuthCookies` entry point, decode the base64url payload of each token independently and accept a finite numeric expiry and compute max(0, floor(exp − serverTimeMs / 1000)). Treat an absent or nonnumeric expiry as unavailable. Use a nonnegative Max-Age capped at the remaining lifetime. Decoding is only a scheduling hint. Identity and refresh decisions still require the existing upstream endpoints. Preserve the cookie names, path, httpOnly, secure and each sameSite value. A missing token still produces no write for that cookie. For compatibility with an opaque or malformed token whose expiry is unavailable, retain the existing fallback age for that cookie (900 or 604800 seconds). An opaque access cookie remains present for SSR eligibility.

Already-issued cookies may have the old Max-Age. On the existing eligible HTML GET path, consider an access cookie with a decodable expired JWT equivalent to an absent access cookie for refresh scheduling. Keep the existing request exclusions, refresh-cookie requirement, one upstream refresh call and request-cookie replacement before SSR. The original age of a refresh cookie that the browser has already discarded cannot be extended retroactively.

**Interface** — Preserve the existing `setAuthCookies(event, data): void`, `shouldRefreshSession(event): boolean` and `withAuthCookies(cookieHeader, tokens): string` entry points. Share the expiry reader from server/utils/api.ts with server/utils/session-refresh.ts; the spec prescribes no new public signature. An expired JWT yields zero remaining cookie lifetime. An unavailable upstream refresh uses the web middleware’s existing transient-failure behavior.

**Scope** — In: existing api.ts cookie setter, session-refresh.ts eligibility helper and the three server specs named below; preserve middleware request-header replacement and upstream identity checks. Out: CLI credential cleanup, ticket defaults and CLI login classification. Changing API token issuance, revocation policy or deployment configuration.

**Verification seam** — US-001 exercises the real cookie setter and SSR middleware with a fixed clock. For the expiry cases in session-refresh.spec.ts, wire the mocked functions to their real implementations (for example via Jest requireActual). Keep H3 and upstream boundaries controlled, and verify the rotated token on the same SSR request. Extend apps/web/tests/server/auth-cookie-samesite.spec.ts, apps/web/tests/server/session-refresh-utils.spec.ts and apps/web/tests/server/session-refresh.spec.ts rather than creating files.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a fixed server clock and access/refresh JWTs expiring in 300/1209600 seconds, when the real setAuthCookies runs, then koda_token and koda_refresh have respective Max-Ages 300 and 1209600. (Spec AC-1.)
When setAuthCookies writes access and refresh cookies, then both are httpOnly, secure and scoped to '/', with sameSite='lax' for access and sameSite='strict' for refresh. (Spec AC-1.)
Given default 15-minute and seven-day JWTs at issue time, when setAuthCookies runs, then the respective Max-Ages are 900 and 604800 seconds. (Spec AC-2.)
When setAuthCookies receives an expired JWT, then its cookie is emitted with Max-Age zero. (Spec AC-2 and failure handling.)
When an access or refresh token is missing, then setAuthCookies produces no cookie write for that token's name. (Spec AC-2.)
Given an opaque access token and a valid refresh JWT, when setAuthCookies runs, then only the access cookie uses the 900-second fallback while refresh uses its own JWT lifetime. (Spec AC-3.)
When setAuthCookies receives an opaque refresh token, then its refresh cookie uses the 604800-second fallback. (Spec AC-3.)

Given a protected HTML GET at minute six with an old 15-minute access cookie containing a five-minute JWT and a valid refresh cookie, when the real SSR middleware runs, then exactly one upstream refresh supplies the rotated access cookie to that same request consumed by SSR. (Spec AC-4.)
Given the same HTML GET at minute four, when the real SSR middleware runs, then it makes zero upstream refresh calls. (Spec AC-5.)
Given only a valid refresh cookie on eligible HTML navigation, when the real SSR middleware runs, then the session rotates on that request. (Spec AC-5.)
Given an API request with the same refresh-only credentials, when the real SSR middleware runs, then it makes zero upstream refresh calls. (Spec AC-5.)
Given an opaque access cookie and a refresh cookie on an otherwise eligible HTML GET, when the real SSR middleware runs, then it makes zero upstream refresh calls. (Spec AC-6.)
When setAuthCookies receives a JWT with string-valued exp, then that cookie uses its existing per-cookie fallback age. (Spec AC-6.)
Given an eligible HTML GET at exactly the numeric access expiry and a refresh cookie, when the real SSR middleware runs, then it requests upstream refresh. (Spec AC-6.)
Given expired access on an eligible HTML GET, when upstream refresh returns 503, then the middleware preserves the incoming cookies. (Spec AC-6.)

Given expired access on an eligible HTML GET, when upstream refresh is unavailable through a transport failure, then the middleware preserves incoming cookies under its existing transient-failure behavior. (Spec failure handling.)

routing.reasoning: A bounded expiry reader and eligibility update reuse the existing cookie setter and SSR refresh path without a new integration; session/token security still requires strict three-session isolation.

modifiedFiles.reason: read each token’s expiry when setting its cookie and share the expiry reader with SSR.
qualify an expired legacy access cookie for eligible SSR refresh.
exercise lifetimes, expiry fallback and existing cookie attributes through the real setter.
cover eligible HTML requests with expired or unexpired JWT cookies.

use the real eligibility and header-replacement helpers in the expiry cases instead of the existing constant stubs; keep H3 and upstream boundaries controlled, and verify the rotated token on the same SSR request.

userStories.title: Clear only the credential used for logout
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry credential provenance through context resolution so successful logout clears only the matching saved credential for the deployment actually used.

**Motivation** — In the CLI, a successful logout with deployment B’s temporary token erases deployment A’s global key.

**Approach** — `resolveContext` resolves key and endpoint independently. Record the key’s winning source (flag, environment, selected named profile, or global) at resolution time. A stored key’s owning endpoint is the API base URL recorded with that entry, with the existing default base URL for a global config lacking a URL. A selected stored profile without a usable owning URL cannot establish ownership and stays untouched. Compare full normalized API bases, retaining path prefixes and nondefault ports, allowing equivalent trailing slashes and the optional trailing `/api` used by the client. In-memory flag/environment credentials own no persistent entry. Keep project-local key and endpoint fields excluded from resolution.

Following successful `authControllerLogout()`, clear only an eligible stored entry whose source, key value and owning endpoint match the credential actually used. Recheck current stored value and endpoint before the edit so a replacement saved during the request survives. Clear a selected profile’s key to an empty string and retain its endpoint and name, so a later request with that profile selected cannot fall through to the global key. Preserve unrelated entries and the global URL. On endpoint mismatch or for a transient credential, skip local mutation. Describe acceptance of the logout request and the actual local action in human output and help. Leave the extent of server-side revocation to the API, including its legacy fallback. JSON success retains `{success:true}`.

**Interface** — The baseline `ResolvedContext` has projectSlug, apiKey and apiUrl. US-002 extends the result of `resolveContext` with credential provenance, retaining the three original fields and independent precedence rules. It preserves the distinction between an empty stored key and a missing one. US-003 extends that same result with optional project defaults. `withContext` already returns the resolver result intact after configuring the client. Logout consumes that returned snapshot once and compares the current stored entry after the remote call. Ticket creation uses the same snapshot for flags and defaults. The public logout command itself has no key flag: verify flag provenance at the resolver/helper seam.

Failed remote logout performs no local edit.

**Scope** — In: provenance and conditional cleanup in config.ts, the existing withContext seam, logout action/output/help in commands/auth.ts and their existing specs. Out: ticket-default resolution (US-003), browser expiry (US-001) and login error classification (US-004). Changing API token issuance, revocation policy or deployment configuration. Editing generated client files or migrating the stored profile format. Adding cross-process locking to the shared CLI configuration file. Logout rechecks the current entry after the HTTP request using the existing synchronous store operations.

**Verification seam** — US-002 drives the logout action through real context resolution and observes the endpoint, bearer and persisted config. Replace the unconditional global-clear expectation in auth.spec.ts with isolated credential-store scenarios; capture configured endpoint/bearer at the generated authControllerLogout boundary, then inspect the store after success or rejection. Exercise independent key/URL precedence, complete normalized base comparison and current-value/current-URL rechecks in config.spec.ts. Keep synchronous write security protections and do not weaken setConfig's key validation to erase a profile.
acceptanceCriteria: Given saved global A and environment URL/key for B, when logout obtains its context through withContext, then authControllerLogout is called against B using B's bearer, including when the environment key equals A's saved key. (Spec AC-1.)
Given saved global A and environment URL/key for B, when remote logout succeeds, then the persisted config has zero mutations, including when the environment key equals A's saved key. (Spec AC-1.)
Given selected profile B, when logout to B succeeds, then only B's key becomes an empty string, preserving its name/URL, A's global key and another profile intact. (Spec AC-2.)
Given profile B was cleared by successful logout and remains selected, when resolveContext runs again, then it returns an empty apiKey rather than the global key. (Spec AC-2.)
Given the global credential is used against its owning endpoint, when remote logout succeeds, then only the global key is cleared, preserving the global URL and unrelated entries. (Spec AC-3.)

Given the global stored API base ends in '/api' and the used base is its equivalent bare or trailing-slash form, when logout succeeds, then conditional cleanup identifies the same endpoint and clears only the global key. (Spec AC-3.)

Given a stored credential is selected but an endpoint override changes its host, nondefault port or base path, when remote logout succeeds, then the persisted config has zero local edits for each mismatch. (Spec AC-4.)
Given a stored config, when authControllerLogout rejects, then the action preserves that complete config and reports failure. (Spec AC-5 and failure handling.)
Given a selected stored credential, when its current key or owning URL is replaced while logout is pending and the remote call then succeeds, then cleanup preserves the replacement. (Spec AC-5.)
When non-JSON logout succeeds, then its human-readable output identifies whether a global key, a named profile key or no saved credential was cleared. (Spec AC-6.)
When logout succeeds with --json, then its success output parses as exactly {"success":true}. (Spec AC-6.)
Given resolveContext receives a flag-supplied key equal to the saved global key, when conditional cleanup runs with that snapshot, then the persisted global entry survives. (Spec AC-7.)
Given a selected profile has an empty stored URL but resolution found a usable global endpoint, when logout succeeds, then the selected profile entry stays untouched. (Spec AC-7.)
When Commander's logout help is displayed, then it describes the logout request without promising revocation of all outstanding tokens or containing the credential value. (Spec AC-8.)

When the non-JSON logout success action runs, then its response describes the accepted logout request without promising revocation of all outstanding tokens or containing the credential value. (Spec AC-8.)

routing.reasoning: Provenance, normalized endpoint comparison and synchronous post-request rechecks are bounded changes to the existing config and logout modules, with no locking or new integration; credential mutation requires the security strategy.

modifiedFiles.reason: track key provenance and implement conditional cleanup of the correct persisted entry.
pass the logout context into cleanup after remote success, report the local action and update the help text that currently promises revocation of all tokens.
exercise independent key and URL precedence, endpoint normalization and preservation of replaced credentials.

replace the unconditional global-clear expectation. Exercise real context resolution and credential cleanup against an isolated credential store; capture the configured API call, then assert stored values for success and rejection.

userStories.title: Apply project defaults during ticket creation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve project ticket type and priority defaults through the shared context and apply per-field flag precedence before ticket validation and creation.

**Motivation** — Initializing a project with TASK/HIGH still requires an explicit type to create a ticket and omits HIGH from the request.

**Approach** — Expose the nearest project config’s optional ticket defaults through the same context lookup used by ticket creation. Resolve each field independently using the explicit flag first, then that field’s project default. Run existing type/priority validation on the effective values and send those validated values through `ticketsControllerCreate`. Keep the existing missing-title and missing-type validation when no usable value is supplied. An absent priority leaves it unspecified for the API. Existing configs without defaults remain supported.

**Interface** — The baseline `ResolvedContext` has projectSlug, apiKey and apiUrl. US-002 extends the result of `resolveContext` with credential provenance, retaining the three original fields and independent precedence rules. It preserves the distinction between an empty stored key and a missing one. US-003 extends that same result with optional project defaults. `withContext` already returns the resolver result intact after configuring the client. Logout consumes that returned snapshot once and compares the current stored entry after the remote call. Ticket creation uses the same snapshot for flags and defaults. The public logout command itself has no key flag: verify flag provenance at the resolver/helper seam.

Use the existing init shape `{"projectSlug":"my-project","defaults":{"type":"TASK","priority":"HIGH"}}`; no new function signature is prescribed. Invalid effective ticket inputs exit 3 before an API write.

**Scope** — In: optional defaults on ProjectConfig/ResolvedContext in config.ts, field-specific effective values in commands/ticket.ts and existing config/ticket specs. Out: credential provenance and cleanup implementation (US-002), browser expiry (US-001) and login error classification (US-004). Preserve US-002's metadata and independent resolution precedence. Changing ticket enums, init flags or the CLI exit-code contract. Editing generated client files or migrating the stored profile format. Project-local apiKey/apiUrl remain excluded; the historical project-config document does not override H10.

**Verification seam** — US-003 drives the ticket action from project configuration through the generated-client request boundary. In ticket.spec.ts connect the existing resolver mock to the real resolver for the default cases, using an isolated init-shaped project fixture and controlled credentials. Capture the generated request and use a terminating exit double or subprocess for validation cases, since the default exit spy returns. Extend config.spec.ts for project configurations with and without defaults; read init.ts and docs/specs/SPEC-project-cli-config.md for the saved defaults shape without changing init behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a valid stored credential and nearest project config {"projectSlug":"my-project","defaults":{"type":"TASK","priority":"HIGH"}}, when ticket create is invoked with only a title, then ticketsControllerCreate is called once for my-project with that title, type TASK and priority HIGH. (Spec AC-1.)
Given project defaults TASK/HIGH, when ticket create supplies explicit --type BUG, then the generated-client request contains BUG/HIGH. (Spec AC-2.)
Given project defaults TASK/HIGH, when ticket create supplies explicit --priority LOW, then the generated-client request contains TASK/LOW. (Spec AC-2.)
Given an older project config without defaults, when ticket create supplies an explicit type and title, then creation succeeds with no serialized priority. (Spec AC-3.)

Given a valid stored credential and an older project config without defaults, when ticket create supplies a title but omits type, then it exits 3 using the existing missing-type validation before any create call. (Spec AC-3 and failure handling.)

Given a valid stored credential and an older project config without defaults, when ticket create supplies a valid type but omits title, then it exits 3 using the existing missing-title validation before any create call. (Spec AC-3 and failure handling.)

Given a valid stored credential, title and otherwise valid inputs, when ticket create selects unsupported project default type ALIEN, then it exits 3 before any create call. (Spec AC-4 and failure handling.)

Given a valid stored credential, title and otherwise valid inputs, when ticket create selects unsupported project default priority URGENT, then it exits 3 before any create call. (Spec AC-4 and failure handling.)
Given an invalid project default type, when ticket create supplies a valid explicit type flag and otherwise valid inputs, then the generated-client request sends the valid flag value. (Spec AC-4.)

Given an invalid project default priority, when ticket create supplies a valid explicit priority flag and otherwise valid inputs, then the generated-client request sends the valid flag value. (Spec AC-4.)

Given a valid stored credential, title and otherwise valid effective inputs, when ticket create supplies an unsupported explicit type or priority flag, then it exits 3 before any create call rather than falling back to that field's valid project default. (Spec failure handling: invalid effective ticket inputs.)

userStories.title: Classify login failures from API envelopes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reuse the shared error normalizer so login distinguishes actual API rejections from transport failures without overwriting credentials on failure.

**Motivation** — Login with an invalid key prints `Could not reach API: [object Object]` for a response the API actually delivered.

**Approach** — `agentsControllerFindMe` uses the generated client, which throws the parsed HTTP error body. Reuse the shared CLI error normalizer in `utils/error.ts` for recognized application codes and legacy HTTP-status fields. Login maps normalized 401/403 to the existing invalid-key error, retaining the status. Other known HTTP failures retain their status/message. For an unrecognized numeric application error code with an API message, show that message as an API failure. Actual transport errors keep the transient connectivity diagnostic. The CLI continues to save credentials only after successful validation.

**Interface** — The existing `getStatusAndMessage(err)` in utils/error.ts returns a numeric status or undefined together with a message. US-004 makes this existing result available to login and preserves plain transport Error handling. A numeric nonzero ret can identify a rejected application envelope even when the status mapping has no entry. A known application code takes precedence over conflicting legacy status fields, as it does in the shared normalizer.

Existing helper signature to export without changing its result: `getStatusAndMessage(err: unknown): { status: number | undefined; message: string }`. Preserve `loginCommand(apiKey, apiUrl, options): Promise<LoginResult>` and `loginError(err: unknown): Error & { status?: number; transient?: boolean }`. A failed login leaves the previous credentials available and retains the command’s existing nonzero exit behavior.

**Scope** — In: expose the existing normalizer from utils/error.ts, use it in commands/login.ts and extend the existing login specs; review index.ts to preserve its output and exit behavior. Out: stored-credential provenance/logout cleanup (US-002), project ticket defaults (US-003) and web sessions (US-001). Editing generated client files or migrating the stored profile format. Changing ticket enums, init flags or the CLI exit-code contract.

**Verification seam** — US-004 drives login through its existing credential check and verifies config writes. Drive login.spec.ts with the generated client’s actual error-envelope shape and transport and success controls. Keep any output-module mock at the presentation boundary so the real shared normalizer executes. Assert known ret precedence against conflicting legacy status fields, unknown numeric rejection messages without transient=true, no configuration writes on rejection and exactly one successful credential save using the normalized endpoint. Preserve shared handleApiError semantics for other commands.
acceptanceCriteria: When agentsControllerFindMe rejects login validation with {ret:40000,message:'Unauthorized'}, then login rejects with 'Invalid API key' and status 401 without any config writes. (Spec AC-1.)
When agentsControllerFindMe rejects login validation with application code 40003, then login rejects with 'Invalid API key' and status 403 without any config writes. (Spec AC-1.)
When login validation rejects with a legacy error carrying statusCode 500 and a message, then login's rejection retains that status and message. (Spec AC-2.)
When login validation rejects with an unknown numeric nonzero application code and an API message, then login reports that API message without setting the transient flag. (Spec AC-2.)

Given saved credentials, when login validation throws a transport Error carrying ECONNREFUSED, then the rejection contains the existing 'Could not reach API: ' connectivity diagnostic with the transport reason and transient=true, leaving the saved credentials untouched. (Spec AC-3.)
When credential validation succeeds, then login saves the supplied key and normalized endpoint once. (Spec AC-4.)
When credential validation succeeds, then login returns the existing success message 'Login successful. Credentials saved.'. (Spec AC-4.)
Given validation rejects with ret 40000 and conflicting statusCode 500, when login and the real getStatusAndMessage process the rejection, then both select mapped status 401. (Spec AC-5.)
Given a previously stored key and validation rejects with ret 40000 and conflicting statusCode 500, when login fails, then the previous key remains stored. (Spec AC-5.)

Given previously saved credentials, when credential validation fails through an API rejection, then login leaves those credentials available and the public login command retains its existing exit code 2. (Spec failure handling; existing login catch exit.)

routing.reasoning: Exporting an existing normalizer and adapting login is a bounded change, but credential validation and save-on-success behavior require the security override.

modifiedFiles.reason: expose the existing status/message normalizer for login.
distinguish API rejections from transport errors in the login flow.

drive login with the generated client’s actual error-envelope shape and transport and success controls. Keep any output-module mock at the presentation boundary so the real shared normalizer executes.

analysis:
Repository discovery and architecture: codebase-memory MCP is not exposed in this session, so navigation fell back to direct Read, Glob and Grep tools against the supplied repository root. Read the app source-of-truth contexts before exploration. This is an enhancement of existing code, not greenfield. Despite the supplied package detection labeling web Next.js, it is Nuxt 4 SSR with Nitro/H3 server handlers and Jest: apps/web/package.json:6, apps/web/package.json:33, apps/web/package.json:62. The CLI uses Commander, conf and Jest (apps/cli/package.json:20, apps/cli/package.json:30, apps/cli/package.json:41). Its actual generated client uses fetch-style configuration and throwOnError, not the Axios runtime mentioned in older guidance (apps/cli/src/generated/client.gen.ts:16, apps/cli/src/generated/client/client.gen.ts:198). Keep both clients thin; no API contract, generated SDK, token issuance or business-rule changes are needed. The review documents the synthetic reproductions and their limits at docs/20261120-review-37b396c49.md:31 and docs/20261120-review-37b396c49.md:55; passing baseline suites did not exercise these seams.

US-001 current flow and impact: apps/web/server/utils/api.ts:24 defines koda_token/koda_refresh; setAuthCookies at :39 writes httpOnly, secure, path=/ cookies with access sameSite=lax and refresh sameSite=strict but fixed 900/604800-second ages at :49 and :59. Extend this existing file with a reusable safe base64url JWT expiry reader, independently decode each token, reject non-finite/non-numeric exp as unavailable, and compute max(0, floor(exp - Date.now()/1000)) rather than imposing the old durations on valid JWTs. Only unavailable expiry uses the existing per-cookie fallback; expired numeric expiry is zero, not fallback. Decoding must not establish identity or validate signatures. The API already configures separate access/refresh lifetimes at apps/api/src/config/auth.config.ts:66 and apps/api/src/auth/auth.module.ts:126, so deriving expiry avoids duplicating environment configuration in web. Missing token behavior and all cookie attributes remain unchanged. Consumers of the common setter include login (apps/web/server/api/auth/login.post.ts:19), registration (apps/web/server/api/auth/register.post.ts:19), explicit refresh (apps/web/server/api/auth/refresh.post.ts:26), invitation acceptance (apps/web/server/api/invites/[token]/accept.post.ts:29) and SSR refresh (apps/web/server/middleware/session-refresh.ts:27); these inherit the fix without endpoint rewrites.

US-001 SSR seam and tests: shouldRefreshSession at apps/web/server/utils/session-refresh.ts:29 currently checks HTML GET, excludes API/Nuxt paths, then requires an absent access cookie and present refresh cookie at :39. Treat only a decodable numerically expired access JWT as equivalent to absent; opaque/malformed or string-exp access cookies remain present. Compare server time at the exact expiry boundary without confusing floor-rounded cookie scheduling with identity. withAuthCookies at :43 preserves unrelated request cookies. The middleware makes one refresh call (:7), clears on definite auth failure (:12), preserves transient upstream failures (:16, :33), and replaces event.node.req.headers.cookie before SSR (:28). Preserve those paths. The identity route at apps/web/server/api/auth/me.get.ts:9 and :22 still relies on upstream authorization, and apps/web/middleware/auth.global.ts:15 then :30 decides protected-route access. Do not work around expiry by trusting decoded JWT claims in either identity handler. Modify api.ts, session-refresh.ts and the three existing server specs, changing the middleware itself only if necessary to preserve the integration. apps/web/tests/server/auth-cookie-samesite.spec.ts:7 currently tests attributes using opaque tokens; expand through the real setter with a fixed clock. apps/web/tests/server/session-refresh-utils.spec.ts:19 covers the real helper and :35 cookie merging. Crucially, apps/web/tests/server/session-refresh.spec.ts:9 delegates helper imports to global mocks, and :73-74 currently substitutes constant eligibility/replacement results: expiry cases must delegate to the real helpers, e.g. requireActual, not merely assert mock outputs. Its controlled H3 serializer at :28 and real setter wrappers at :81 can remain. Verify the same SSR request sees rotated access, minute-four/minute-six/exact-expiry controls, exclusion controls, opaque/string-exp fallback, and upstream 503/network preservation. No layout, navigation, theme or UI text changes are intended.

US-002 resolution and storage: apps/cli/src/config.ts:59 defines the three-field ResolvedContext, resolveContext at :137 resolves project config once then global config. URL precedence uses truthiness (:165), while key precedence uses nullish selection (:172); preserve their independence and the distinction between an empty stored key and missing key. Project-local apiKey/apiUrl are deliberately ignored with a warning at :153, and findProjectConfig at :224 walks to the nearest file with a homedir ceiling at :231; neither security boundary may regress. Capture winning key provenance during resolution, including the selected profile name and its stored owning endpoint, instead of guessing from key equality afterward. Global ownership uses its recorded URL or DEFAULT_API_URL at :132; a profile lacking a usable recorded URL cannot prove ownership even if URL resolution falls back globally. The existing client setup strips terminal /api in apps/cli/src/utils/context.ts:49, then configureApiClient sets baseUrl and bearer at apps/cli/src/utils/api-client.ts:13. withContext returns ctx intact at :51; retain the one returned snapshot and use it for logout cleanup.

Replace that call with conditional stored-entry cleanup after authControllerLogout succeeds, reporting global/profile/no-local-edit without printing secrets or overclaiming server revocation. Invalid selected defaults must fail locally with exit 3, whereas a valid flag overrides an invalid default for that field. Modify config.ts, ticket.ts and existing config/ticket specs only; read init.ts and docs/specs/SPEC-project-cli-config.md:28 for fixture shape, not as authority to restore project-local credentials.
